question.text: A body is projected vertically upward from the ground with a launch speed u. It crosses an elevation of 80 m at two different instants, such that the time gap between these two occurrences is 6 s. Calculate the initial speed u. (Take g = 10 m/s²)
conditions: time difference between identical heights = 6 s

figure.description: A sketch illustrating the vertical path of an object thrown upwards from the ground with initial speed u, showing it at a height of 80 m during ascent and descent, with an upward positive sign convention.

solution.approach: Write the height equation as a quadratic in time, use the sum and product of its two roots, and apply the given 6 s gap between them.

steps.text: Write the height reached at time t, taking upward as positive from the ground.
Set the height to 80 m; this gives a quadratic whose two roots t₁ and t₂ are the two times the ball is at that height.
From the quadratic, write the sum and product of the roots in terms of u.
Use (t₂ − t₁)² = (t₁+t₂)² − 4t₁t₂ with the given 6 s gap to solve for u.

common_mistakes.text: Treating the 6 s gap as the single time to reach the height, and solving 80 = 6u − 5(6)² for u, giving about 43.3 m/s.
